servingThisHomeSchools.name: Peggy Heller Elementary School
servingThisHomeSchools.fullAddress: 201 Lake View Dr, City of Atwater, CA 95301

schoolReviews.review: Oh today was tryouts but the lady didn’t let the others because of there shoes and my mom didn’t get it from parents square

I agree with the previous review. The principal at this school doesn’t care about the children, she only cares about herself. I am glad she is out from Peggy Heller unfortunately, she was moved to another school. The bullying from staff and students is ridiculous. There are many staff including a new counselor that supports bullying at this school. Nothing was done when I reached out for support for my child. My child didn’t feel safe and was greatly affected from this school. Don’t get me wrong, there are a few great teachers but there are some bad apples too. I hope that the new principal will change this school’s environment.
School principal needs to be replaced, she has no experience with the new flow of 7th and 8th graders. Many of the parents i consult with want her removed. I am working on a signed petition.

The school really pushes high scores and demands a lot from the children, which can be good and bad. It all depends on how well your relationship is with the teacher, the principal, and if your child can take that type of pressure. The rules on bullies are not absolute either, which is also another huge problem. If a child is thought of as weak, they will always be targeted. The school, teachers, principal nor district did much to stop much of the negative behavior. Shame.

Love this school - I've heard horror stories from parents with kids in other school when their child has problems or may need more assistance and/or testing and every staff member I have come into contact during my sons four years at Peggy Heller has gone above and beyond to ensure he is given every opportunity to do well and succeed. The standards there seem higher but I've seen my child grow more than I thought possible. You can tell that each staff member and the students take pride in their school.

Love Peggy Heller. I have had 2 of my children attend this school and have no complaints what so ever. Definitely the best school in Atwater and I say that from experience. Principle and stuff are very fair and take care of any issues ASAP. Can't wait for my 3rd child to start school.

servingThisHomeSchools.fullAddress: 2201 Fruitland Ave, City of Atwater, CA 95301

schoolReviews.review: This school is performing better than most in the valley. With a diverse group of students its test scores have flourished. The Ag program is the best in the state and has been recognized as such. The Principal is strong and is focused on student involvement. The leadership seems to try new things each year to try to make improvements. As a parent I appreciate the staffs willingness to communicate. My student is involved in many aspects of the school and will be sad to leave upon graduation, but fully prepared for a UC.

they don't even deserve a one in my opinion its the worst school in the area. people are better off going to buhac at least there the staff know how to deal with problems(or from what i've heard) i would reccommend any school over atwater high

schoolsToShowOnDP.fullAddress: 1271 Bellevue Rd, City of Atwater, CA 95301

schoolReviews.review: I felt that both of my students were well taught and prepared to succeed in Junior High School. I know that many former students keep in touch with the teachers at Elmer Wood, and the teachers are always willing to help out. Test scores are high, and the office staff is friendly. A five-star rating is totally deserved!!
I have two children who attended this school, and both had wonderful teachers, ones who stayed engaged with the parents and kept us up to date with how they did in class. Great school.

My two children have attended Elmerwood. My eldest went for kinder-6th and my daughter has been there since k-1 and now in 2nd grade. I have no complains about the school. Love the principal, teachers and staff (after school program helpers) I notice a great difference between my kids and my nephews who attend other schools in the area like Aileen Colburn, Mitchell k-6 and Bellevue school. My kids are by far so much more advanced and in lower grades.

My daughter is in K1 and she loves school, teacher, and friends. Mrs. L does a great job of teaching and encouraging all her students. She is kind The principal is awesome. Mrs. Nelson is very interactive with her students. Overall, when I drop off my child I know she is safe, learning, and being treated fairly.

This school does not support parents. The Principal is overly focused on teachers/staff rights and opposed to parental concerns. The Principal does not take parental concerns seriously. I would definitely think twice about letting your child go to this school. There are other schools to choose from in this district that far outweigh the level of support at this one.

Elmer Wood is a great school. My son loves this school. The teachers are really very helpful and they care about their students. The principal is very nice. My son Paul is in K-1. He likes his teacher. Miss Livinal works hard to help her students to achieve their academic goals. Keep it up! God bless this school.

Great school! The kids are given agendas at the beginning of the year to write their homework in. I believe if you ask the principal you as a parent could help out in the classroom. I know first hand this school does not take bullying lightly. My daughter was bullied by 2 students & I emailed the principal in the morning & it was taken care of & the other parents were notified by that afternoon. The more parents that would get involved the better the school would be. We can't parents to help on the parent club board or volunteer a limitless time. Just like every other thing that's volunteer, you have 20% of the people doing 80% of the work. If you want things to improve then volunteer & help implement changes. I have one child that went K-6th there & one child that has gone K-4th & will be there the next 2 years. Love this school!!!

schoolsToShowOnDP.fullAddress: 1800 N Buhach Rd, City of Atwater, CA 95301

schoolReviews.review: The school does a tremendous job of meeting the needs of students despite being a large school.
Honestly how do I even explain this, they have the right ideas but wrong execution

I graduated in 2016. I can attest to the AP curriculum that it is top notch. Common core has tainted the common core curriculum like a virus but that's every school now. BCHS as of 2015 was ahead in technology in most areas. Chromebooks are used effectively to supplement learning. BCHS has a great band and theater program and is the only high school in Merced County to incorporate an engineering academy as an option. The AP teachetrs are the best you will find. AP Chemistry with Camp is the best chemistry you will find in California. The arts are also excellent, Freitas is a personal favorite as well as, Newton go APUSH. Admin is great although I'm sure it has changed since I have left. BCHS strives for school pride and unity. Thy gyms not bad. Overall its the best high school in the area for sure.
my experience in this school is meh

Well im currently a student at buhach and I thoroughly enjoy the school, the staff are great and funny, especially Mr. Freitas, the school is clean and kept up very well, and is also very well organized, my only issue is that recently we students and staff are being required to wear a photo ID at all times and receive a small punishment if found without one, though it is justified with all the craziness going on in the world.

schoolsToShowOnDP.fullAddress: 1020 E Bellevue Rd, City of Atwater, CA 95301

schoolReviews.review: This school is not a good school I went here and I just graduated recently however I know I am a child, but I also have to say parents do not send your kids here it is not a good school at all.. they dont even punish kids who fight other kids like no suspension instead they just try to fix stuff .. but this is a warning please do not send your kids here thanks for reading my opinion.

This is a warning for Substitute teachers in the 6 through 8 category. The school has no consequences for misbehavior. They talk about it ,but if you send a child out they come right back. If you have values of proper work ethics and manners leave them at home. Admin is anti teacher and has the attitude of "my way or the highway". They expect the Sub to perform all the onerous duties of the regular teacher for their pitiful pay. It is now nearing 3 months and still no pay even though all the requirements that a Sub has to go through have long since been met. I was warned not to sub at this school and foolishly I did so. I spent 35 years in the classroom as a single subject teacher and I always tried to give my subs as easy a time as possible and respect their comments and/or information about the students. Long term subs were given the respect and support due any teacher. It is amazing how many subs left me their contact information. When I was on long term jury duty I tried to lessen the load by giving my sub detailed lesson plans and correcting the student's work. While I had to move I was in 4 different schools and the admin treated subs the way you treat people who are trying to do their best. Do not expect anything but contempt and attitudes of demigods from admin.

This school does not care about your child when it comes to suspension and being wrongfully accused. They are biased based on if your child has a history of fighting as well as, previous conflicts. Nobody matter the past should not be treated with such disrespect. Rather than asking both students for both sides of the story they take advantage based on the past of your student. When my mother who is Hispanic calls the front desk they speak in a belittling tone , I've heard this on numerous calls. I don't reccomend sending your child here.
My daughter has been going here since kindergarten and it is a good school for children to learn and grow.
Love the teachers! Next year I'll be a 7th grader but I'm not sure about those teachers, I know the P.E teacher is really Strict. And also Bellevue has PreSchool and has grades K-8 not K-6

Bad teachers and school didn't do much plus i never gotten an opology from the teachers. My daughter who was attending preschool here with three Spanish teacher. My girl was doing her little business in the restroom and they left to eat breakfast without her not even counting their kids and checking or calling before they leave. They lock her in the dark room. When she was done she came out and started to panicked and ran to the door trying to open it but she couldn't cause it was lock inside and out. She started crying and banging but no one can see. She then told me she went to go sat on the mat and weep. When the Class has return the teachers were all just surprised to see her by herself. I can image how sad and scare my baby girl was.

As a mother who has had to move around alot i've seen my fair share of schools,also my daughter has also been in,for a 5 grader.Bellevue is the best yet,whats more important she likes the school,i comment on this before but I'll do it again.To all schools thank you and for the teacher who can teach a room of 30 or more,you guys are the best

entryPointFlyout.value:
Wind Factor is a tool created by the nonprofit First Street. It uses the First Street National Wind Model, which forecasts how hurricanes and costs from resulting wind damages to structures will change over time due to climate change.

A property's Wind Factor indicates its likelihood to experience extreme winds over the next 30 years, from 1 (minimal) to 10 (extreme). Properties with higher Wind Factor scores are more likely to experience higher winds more frequently today and in the future.

entryPointDescription.value: Based on the likelihood and speed of hurricane, tornado, or severe storm winds reaching this property, it has minimal wind risk.

scoreDescription.value: This property's wind risk is not significantly changing over time.

riskFactorHomeURLText.value: See all wind data on firststreet.org

expandableSummary.value: Minimal risk of a flood reaching the building in the next 30 years

entryPointFlyout.value:
Flood Factor® is a tool created by the nonprofit First Street. It uses the First Street Flood Model, a nationwide, probabilistic flood model that shows a location’s risk of flooding from rain, rivers, tides, and storm surge. It builds off of decades of peer-reviewed research and forecasts how flood risks will change over time due to changes in the environment. Flood Factor is not intended to include all possible risks of flood.

A property's Flood Factor is an indicator of its comprehensive flood risk, ranging from 1 (minimal) to 10 (extreme). Properties with higher Flood Factors are more likely to have flooded in the past, and are more likely to flood in the future.

entryPointDescription.value: Based on this property’s projected likelihood and depth of flooding, it has minimal flood risk.

scoreDescription.value: This property's flood risk is not significantly changing over time.

entrypointGraphFlyout.value: Flood risk accumulates over time. Cumulative risk is calculated to the largest building or center of an empty lot. Raised or elevated buildings may not be as vulnerable as ground-level buildings or buildings with basements.

entrypointGraphDescription.value: This property is unlikely to flood in the next 30 years.

riskFactorHomeURLText.value: See all flood data on firststreet.org

riskSpecificSubsectionFlyout.value:
The FEMA flood zone shown is the most probable estimated zone.

The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) is a government agency that maps flood zones in communities across the US, identifying areas of varying flood risk on Flood Insurance Rate Maps (FIRMs). FEMA creates FIRMs to inform flood insurance pricing in the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) and to guide floodplain management regulations for NFIP-participating communities.

riskSpecificSubsectionFlyout2.value: The FEMA flood zone shown is the most probable zone as estimated by MassiveCert, Inc.

riskSpecificSubsectionDescription.value: This property is estimated to be in FEMA Zone X (unshaded), which is designated as a low-to-moderate risk flood area. In this zone, the risk of flooding is reduced, but not completely removed.

insuranceFlyout.value: To help you understand what it costs to protect this home with flood insurance we've partnered with Neptune Flood. Redfin may receive a commission if you purchase a policy through this link. There may be other flood insurance providers in your area.

insuranceDescription.value:

entryPointFlyout.value:
Fire Factor is a tool created by the nonprofit First Street. It uses the First Street National Wildfire Model's nationwide, behavioral wildfire model that shows a specific location's probabilistic risk of wildfire based on the vegetation, topography, and fire weather in the surrounding area. Fire Factor is not intended to include all possible risks of fire.

A property's Fire Factor indicates its cumulative wildfire risk, ranging from 1 (minimal) to 10 (extreme). Properties with higher Fire Factors are more likely to be in a wildfire in the future.

entryPointDescription.value: Based on this property's distance to wildfire risk areas and burnable vegetation, it has minimal wildfire risk.

scoreDescription.value: This property's fire risk is not significantly changing over time.

entrypointGraphFlyout.value: Wildfire risk accumulates over time, so a property with a 0.1% chance of wildfire this year would have at least a 3% chance of being affected by wildfire at least once within 30 years. Being affected by wildfire refers to any actively burning fuels coming into contact with the largest building on the property.

insuranceFlyout.value: Most homeowners insurance typically includes fire coverage but in some areas, this will need to be purchased separately. Investing in fire insurance is one way to offset the cost of wildfire damage, and can help reduce your financial risk.

entryPointFlyout.value:
Heat Factor is a tool created by the nonprofit First Street. Heat Factor™ uses the First Street Extreme Heat Model to determine property-specific heat risk across the United States. The model is a spatial temperature model that determines a specific location’s exposure to extreme heat events based on the surface temperature, topography, land cover, and humidity in the surrounding area.

A property's Heat Factor indicates its risk of extreme heat exposure over the next thirty years, ranging from 1 (minimal risk) to 10 (extreme risk). Heat Factors are based on the current average daily high temperature and humidity of a property’s specific location during the hottest month of the year, and considers how it’s expected to grow over the next 30 years.

entryPointDescription.value: Based on current and future temperature and humidity in the area and at this specific location, this property has major heat risk.

scoreDescription.value: This property's heat risk is increasing as weather patterns change.

entrypointGraphFlyout.value: This chart shows the number of days exceeding what is considered a hot day at this property. This is defined by using the 98th percentile “feels like” temperature in this area, or the hottest 7 days in the 4km area surrounding this property for a given year and using the lowest “high” temperature from those 7 days as a base. A property may have more or less hot days than the surrounding area depending on its individual exposure to heat.

entrypointGraphDescription.value: A “hot day” in this area is considered to be any day with a “feels like” temperature of 103º. Over the next 30 years, this property is expected to see a 8% increase in the number of hot days per year.

We use your income and monthly debt to come up with your debt-to-income ratio, or DTI. We base your buying power on your DTI. We calculate your buying power based on a DTI of 36%, which is the general rule around how much of your income should go toward debt.

The ranges below will help you understand if you have enough income to live comfortably for the selected home price. A general guide is to budget around 28% of your pre-tax income for your mortgage payment, and another 8% for other debts.

Affordable: 0%-36%
Stretch: 37%-50%
Ambitious: Above 50%
